messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV/P1 - Latency SLO breach detected on /v1/generate (p99 > 3s). Alert rule: router.p99 > 3s for 5m. Pager sent to on-call. Link: https://redwood/ops/incidents/1772509876

sarah.w: Ack, I'm on it. Paging mike.k and kai for routing/lb. Any customer-facing pages yet?

mike.k: oncall here. I see p95 jumped ~800ms -> 1.8s and p99 at 9.4s for the last 10m. Streaming stalls increasing. Which routers are spiking?

kai: Checking router metrics now. Running `curl -s http://router-admin.local/metrics | grep router_shard` to identify hot shards.

kai: Output snippet:```
router_shard_requests_total{shard="s-12",region="us-west-2"} 432187
router_shard_avg_latency_ms{shard="s-12",region="us-west-2"} 1200
router_shard_requests_total{shard="s-03",region="eu-west-1"} 312
router_shard_avg_latency_ms{shard="s-03",region="eu-west-1"} 45
```

kai: s-12 in us-west-2 is ~10x the request volume of other shards. Hot partition.

sarah.w: Any recent deploys to routing or hash policy? eng-runtime?

eng-runtime: We rolled a change to 'consistent-hash-v2' at 02:12 UTC to improve affinity (PR #4129). It changed how key hashing maps user-id -> shard (weighting by region). Rollout to 30% at 02:15, 100% at 02:21.

mike.k: That would explain skew. If the new policy pushes high-traffic keys into s-12, tail will blow. Can we revert to previous policy or temporarily disable affinity?

kai: I can patch router config to fallback to `round_robin` for the affected pool. Proposed commands:```
# preview
rctl route get --pool inference-prod --policy
# set fallback to round robin
rctl route update --pool inference-prod --policy fallback=round_robin --reason "mitigate hot shard" --dry-run=false
```

sarah.w: Do it. Also start draining the unhealthy shard to redistribute inflight sessions:```
kubectl -n router scale deployment router-s-12 --replicas=0 || rctl shard drain s-12
```

ops-bot: Executing: `rctl route update --pool inference-prod --policy fallback=round_robin --reason "mitigate hot shard" --dry-run=false`

ops-bot: Success. New policy applied (id=f7a9). Rolling update to routers starting now.

kai: K8s drain triggered: `router-s-12` scaled down. Watch shows inflight sessions drained from 420 -> 12 -> 0 over 90s.

mike.k: Early signs: p99 dropped from 9.4s -> 600ms within 3m of applying fallback. p95 back to ~350ms. Streaming stalls reduced.

sarah.w: Good. Customer impact: telemetry shows ~18% of active streaming sessions experienced stalls >1s during window 02:10-02:25 UTC. Affected customers: two high-traffic accounts in us-west-2 (cust-A, cust-B). Notify CSE for outreach.

eng-runtime: Root cause hypothesis: consistent-hash-v2 had a bug in the region-weight calc that ignored capacity tags and over-assigned keys to s-12. We'll open an immediate revert PR and a patch to weight computation.

kai: Creating postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime. Command: `gh issue create --title "INCIDENT: router hash policy caused hot shard" --assignee eng-runtime --label incident,sev1`

anika: I'm taking handoff for the next shift at 03:00 UTC. Any outstanding actions?

sarah.w: Action items:
- eng-runtime: revert consistent-hash-v2 and release a fix (high)
- eng-runtime: add unit tests for region weight calc (high)
- runtime/ops: add alert that flags >4x deviation in per-shard QPS within 2m (medium)
- CSE: notify impacted customers and collect session ids for forensics (high)
- oncall: monitor p95/p99 for next 2h and prepare rollback plan (sarah.w -> anika)

anika: Acknowledged. I'll monitor and run canary checks. Please @mention me on updates.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Timeline: 02:12 change roll started, 02:21 full rollout, 02:28 mitigation applied, 02:32 tail improved; P1 -> monitoring.

sarah.w: Final note: No data exfiltration. Customer requests to support routed to CSE. We'll follow up with a postmortem with timeline and metrics. Adding label `postmortem-required`.

mike.k: Reopen if p99 rises above 1s for 5m. Otherwise closing paging loop. Thanks team! :raised_hands:

anika: Taking over watch. Logging in to dashboards now.

ops-bot: Auto-snapshots saved: router-metrics-1772509876-1772515400.tar.gz

sarah.w: Closing thread from on-call perspective, handoff complete.
